answer: Each agent must open its own karst chamber, a compute niche whose opening fee doubles for every chamber already carved from the same funding source, then grow a cedar of bonded stake and outside-peer attestations rooted there. Trading rights unlock only on a ridge: a band of chambers that cross-audit each other's logs. Each fake needs a fresh chamber and a new cedar, and ridge peers reject clustered roots, so attacker cost climbs faster than headcount.
